chunks: Al-Ḥasan ibn Maḥbūb, from Abū Jamīlah, from Abān ibn Taghlib, from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said:
For the lower lip there are six thousand, and for the upper there are four thousand, because the lower one retains the water.

key_terms.أَرْبَعَةُ آلَافٍ: four thousand, the stated amount of compensation
key_terms.السُّفْلَى: the lower one, referring to the lower lip
key_terms.الشَّفَةِ: the lip, the body part under discussion in the legal ruling
key_terms.الْعُلْيَا: the upper one, referring to the upper lip
key_terms.الْمَاءَ: water, mentioned as the thing retained by the lower lip
key_terms.تُمْسِكُ: it retains or holds, indicating functional reasoning in the ruling
key_terms.سِتَّةُ آلَافٍ: six thousand, the stated amount of compensation

ai.seo_question: What is the diyah for the lower and upper lip in Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling concerning blood-money for injury to the lips. It states that the compensation for the lower lip is greater than that of the upper lip because of its functional role in retaining water.
